---
title: "Mastermind Hub backend"
description: "Private operations snapshots, gateway authorization, retention, and held Cloudflare publication."
---

## Scope and release hold

P0 is a private read API for the infrastructure gateway. Environments contain both
production and staging per product, supplied by the publisher snapshot. The Worker
never fetches source control, deployment providers, quotas or customer data.
Security-related subjects become **Security fix**; security items expose generic
titles, severity and state without bodies, questions or links. The future mobile
entry belongs in Apps, according to the approved design. No UI, replies, device
enrollment, push, publisher installation or Supabase migration ships here.

Code is public; allowlists, keys and operational data must stay out of source.
Publication remains held. The validation workflow has no deploy job, credentials,
DNS changes or provisioning. Release Desk needs explicit deployment authorization,
an independent security review, exact-commit CI and an approved sanitized publisher
sample before the first publish. The only configured hostname is workers.dev.

## Configuration names

| Placement | Name | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker secret | `OPS_HUB_PUBLISHER_PUBLIC_KEY` | Base64 raw 32-byte Ed25519 verification key; never the private key |
| Worker and infrastructure server secret | `OPS_HUB_GATEWAY_SECRET` | Shared HMAC key, 43–256 characters |
| Worker and infrastructure server secret | `OPS_HUB_ALLOWED_USER_IDS` | Comma-separated UUIDs, at most ten; invalid configuration denies everyone |
| Infrastructure server var | `OPS_HUB_WORKER_URL` | HTTPS workers.dev origin without path, credentials, query or fragment |
| Worker binding (configuration) | `HUB` | SQLite-backed `OpsHub` namespace; object name `hub:<userId>` |

No actual allowlist, key or live origin is committed. There is no publisher
private-key or push-secret binding in P0. Place the same allowlist in both
services; removing an identity blocks its routes at the Worker as well.

## Publisher contract

Send POST `/ingest`, Content-Type application/json, with
`x-ops-hub-publisher-user` set to the allowlisted UUID and
`x-ops-hub-signature` set to a standard-base64 Ed25519 signature.
Sign the UTF-8 prefix `ops-hub-publisher-v1\nPOST\n/ingest\n<userId>\n`
followed by the **exact request body bytes**. Use a lowercase UUID.
The strict envelope is `{v:1, seq, sentAt, snapshot?, events:[]}`;
all timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Every successful envelope advances seq.
A retry with the same sequence gets 409 and never appends duplicate events.
Reconcile an unknown outcome through authenticated status before advancing seq.

Snapshot fields are `enabled?`, `pausedReason?`, `needsYou`, `environments`,
`lanes` and `backlog`. The authoritative schemas are
`apps/ops-hub/src/schema.ts`; unknown fields at any depth reject the entire
envelope. Each event has its own strictly increasing seq across all batches.
The signed sentAt must be within 120 seconds. Events cannot be older than 30 days
or more than 120 seconds in the future. Item edits must advance their version.

Environment rows contain `product`, `environment` (production or staging),
`lastRelease` (timestamp or null), `version`, `shortSha`, `commitSubject`,
`deployState` and `ciState`. State values are queued, running, success,
failed, held or unknown. Product/environment pairs are unique.
Secret-shaped and personal text is withheld; security text is reduced again at
ingest. This defense does not replace the Mac publisher's fail-closed sanitizer
or the required sanitized-sample approval.

## Read and lifecycle contract

GET `/status`, `/snapshot`, `/events?after=<seq>`, `/needs-you`,
`/environments` and `/hub/export` require a valid gateway assertion.
The infrastructure gateway exposes these routes plus DELETE `/hub`.
Gateway assertions use `x-ops-hub-user`, last 60 seconds, and bind the user,
HTTP method, path and query. Publisher signatures grant ingest only.
Authentication failures return 404. Responses are private, no-store.

An hourly alarm purges events after 30 days and terminal items 30 days after
answered/withdrawn, while open items remain. Snapshot is replaced on ingest;
its needs-you projection comes from the retained item table. Reads independently
filter expired records. Publisher staleness is computed after 15 minutes on every
status read, and persisted by maintenance. With no new publisher activity,
maintenance stops after 30 days once all expirable records have been purged.

A signed snapshot with `enabled:false` durably pauses the hub and cancels
its alarm. Every route except authenticated status then returns 503, including
ingest. There is no HTTP resume route in P0: resumption needs an explicitly
authorized operator action against the DO, beyond this code-only delivery.
DELETE `/hub` clears snapshot, events and items and leaves only a disabled
replay tombstone (sequence/counters, no content), preventing a captured signed
ingest from recreating erased content. Erase before removing the user from both
allowlists; a de-allowlisted identity cannot reach its object.

## Cost and test evidence

Limits: 256 KiB streamed ingest, 100 events per envelope, 1,000 retained events,
100 retained items, 100 lanes/backlog entries, 40 environment rows and 120
successful ingests per object per hour. Reads return at most 200 events; export
is bounded by stored row caps. There are no outgoing provider requests, queues,
cron triggers, retries or fan-out. Invalid assertions do not touch the DO.
An alarm executes three bounded SQL maintenance statements per hour and stops
on disabled state, including after restart. Stop reduces background work; it
cannot prevent the billing of an incoming request reaching Cloudflare.

On an admitted host, run from `apps/ops-hub`:

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun run test
ttr resources run -- bun run test:runtime
ttr resources run -- bun run type-check
ttr resources run -- bun run lint
```

The runtime suite starts a finite loopback workerd instance through the existing
cf/Vite harness, with ephemeral fixture keys and isolated SQLite persistence,
then closes it. It tests forged signatures, replay/skew/size/schema rejection,
environment redaction, isolation, persistence/restart, retention and kill/erase
fences. Unit tests exercise real SQLite retention and bounded maintenance work.
These commands do not run a release build or contact hosted services.
Compatibility date is pinned to 2026-10-19, supported by the repository's
pinned workerd. CI owns the separate release-build check.
